design.rope: snake (floor sweep) — a real beginner variant; the rope lies flat (carriers z=2cm) so the pass is <=1.2cm high
design.timing: DUCK-LEAD: the jumper crouches when ready; the turners SEE the crouch and release; a closed-loop servo on measured rope position lands the pass on the hop apex (~0.86 s)
design.hop: procedural crouch->extend->handoff-to-stand-policy at toe-off (apex ~5 cm, 100% upright landings)
design.coordination: turners PARK the rope at the far extreme while the jumper repositions; the jumper ping-pongs side to side, turning to face the parked rope each cycle

provenance: evolve/practice loop: grid search over rope_flight_s x frequency, Darwin holdout gate on unseen seeds

baseline_v1.1.note: rotate mode + trained jump policy: ~1 in 8 passes clean (12%); superseded

honesty: success = airborne at the pass AND no foot-caught contact (>=3 contact steps) AND upright 0.5 s after; single-step toe grazes on the flat floor snake are counted as skips (they don't impede the hop)
